world.h: Brazil's presidential race heads to a runoff
world.b: Flávio Bolsonaro took 47% and President Lula 45% in Sunday's first round, so the two meet in a runoff on October 25.
more: Flávio Bolsonaro is the son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, who is under house arrest after a conviction for plotting a coup.

world.h: Iran says Strait of Hormuz stays closed
world.b: Tehran said the waterway will stay closed until the US meets conditions from their June agreement in Islamabad.
more: Iran's demands include ending the war, lifting blockades and sanctions, releasing frozen assets and paying compensation.
Iran also said there is no military solution to its conflict with the US.

world.h: US pulls B-1 bombers from British base
world.b: The US moved all 12 B-1 bombers out of RAF Fairford after new warnings of an Iranian-backed plot.
more: British police arrested five men near the base the week before.

world.h: Spain calls snap election amid housing protests
world.b: Tens of thousands marched in Madrid and other cities over housing, and Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez called elections for November 29.
more: Lawmakers had rejected his housing measures.

world.h: Hundreds of French high schools shut by protests
world.b: About 500 French high schools are closed as students protest teacher shortages, crowded classrooms and run-down buildings.
more: Authorities have arrested more than 5,000 people since the protests began, about 85% of them minors.

national.h: Judge halts border wall work in Big Bend
national.b: Federal Judge Kathleen Cardone blocked further border wall construction inside Big Bend National Park.
more: She signaled that constitutional claims against the wall are likely to succeed.

national.h: Tennessee prison chief resigns after execution
national.b: Frank Strada is stepping down after the botched execution attempt of Christa Pike, who remains in critical condition.
more: Democracy Now! reports it was his fifth failed execution in two states since 2022.

national.b: Cornell President Michael Kotlikoff welcomed an independent law firm investigation into a 2024 gang rape case.
more: The New York attorney general is also running a criminal investigation.

national.h: Search ends for six aboard crashed medical jet
national.b: The Coast Guard suspended its search for six people aboard a medical jet that crashed on a flight from Bermuda to Boston.

politics.h: Trump names Jay Clayton AI czar
politics.b: President Trump picked Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton to lead a new 'Super Intelligence Force' for federal AI work.
more: An OpenAI safety staffer, David Robinson, recently resigned saying the company 'isn't being nearly careful enough.'

politics.h: KKK tries to rebrand as the 'Knights Party'
politics.b: The hate group is trying to rebrand itself as the Knights Party to grow its base, Al Jazeera reports.

politics.h: Despair fuels political anxiety among students
politics.b: College students' worry about the future is fueling restlessness with a political system they fear can't improve, PBS reports.

international.h: Yemen's government opens offensive on Houthis
international.b: Saudi-backed government forces announced an operation to retake areas including the capital, Sana'a.
more: The Houthis answered with missile and drone attacks on Saudi Aramco sites over the weekend.

international.b: Ethiopian federal forces recaptured Mekelle, the capital of Tigray, amid renewed fighting.
more: Four African leaders issued a joint declaration as the war escalates.

international.h: Nearly 1,500 migrants sent from Malaysia to Myanmar
international.b: Myanmar received nearly 1,500 migrants returned from Malaysia despite UN warnings.

international.h: Gaza airstrike kills at least five
international.b: An Israeli airstrike on a Gaza City apartment building killed at least five Palestinians, including four women.
more: About 1,400 Palestinians have been killed in Gaza since last October's ceasefire, Democracy Now! reports.

international.b: Police detained at least 700 people in Delhi as the youth-led movement demanded the chief election commissioner resign.
more: Protesters object to tens of millions of people being removed from voter rolls.
Authorities imposed an internet shutdown.

international.h: Imran Khan supporters march on Islamabad
international.b: Supporters of jailed former Prime Minister Imran Khan began a mass march after talks with the government failed.

international.h: Singapore turns matchmaker as births fall
international.b: Singapore is launching matchmaking efforts to address its very low birth rate.

business.h: OPEC+ keeps oil output steady for November
business.b: Seven major oil exporters, including Saudi Arabia and Russia, agreed to keep production steady in November as Brent crude stayed above $100 a barrel.

science.h: First miniature quasar aimed at Earth spotted
science.b: Astronomers report finding microblazars, small versions of blazars that point at Earth.
more: They may produce some of the mysterious ultra-high-energy cosmic particles that reach Earth.

science.h: Nobel medicine prize goes to optogenetics pioneers
science.b: Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel won the 2026 Nobel Prize in physiology or medicine for work on light-gated ion channels and optogenetics.

sports.b: Atlanta beat Los Angeles 3-2 on Sunday to tie their National League Division Series at one game each.
Milwaukee beat San Diego 4-3 on Sunday for a 2-0 lead in their NL Division Series.

sports.h: White Sox and Rays take ALDS openers
sports.b: The White Sox blanked Cleveland 3-0 and Tampa Bay edged the Yankees 1-0 in Saturday's AL Division Series openers.

goodnews.h: Man catches child who fell from balcony in Egypt
goodnews.b: Video shows a man in Egypt rushing to catch a young boy who fell from a second-floor balcony.
more: The child hit a washing line on the way down, giving the man crucial extra time to reach him.

goodnews.h: Dakar neighbours clean up school for new year
goodnews.b: Students, teachers and volunteers in Dakar, Senegal, cleaned Medina Gounass Elementary School on Saturday ahead of the new academic year.
more: They swept classrooms, cleared drains and removed plastic and household waste.
Organizers said the effort also aimed to raise awareness about protecting the environment.

local.h: Mamdani to clear 10,000 families off childcare waitlist
local.b: The city will clear 10,000 families from the subsidized childcare waitlist after the program ran out of money.
more: More than 16,000 families are waiting for help.

local.h: Two killed in Queens and Brooklyn crashes
local.b: A 62-year-old died in a hit-and-run Monday and a 23-year-old died in a crash involving an impaired driver Sunday.

local.h: NY's stockpiled abortion pills have all expired
local.b: New York bought 150,000 misoprostol pills in 2023 for $112,000, and the whole supply has expired.
more: The Department of Health plans to destroy the reserve.

local.h: Legionnaires' outbreaks spark NYC water debate
local.b: Groups backed by cooling tower companies propose citywide drinking water filtration; some experts doubt it's needed.

local.h: City Council hearing to spotlight AI risks
local.b: The City Council will hear from four tech workers and whistleblowers about the dangers of AI.

local.h: Sixth person dies after falling ill in NYPD custody
local.b: A 54-year-old man died after becoming ill following his arrest Friday, the sixth in-custody death this year.

periods.name: Monday
periods.text: Sunny, with a high near 69. Breezy, with a northwest wind 16 to 21 mph in the afternoon.

periods.name: Monday Night
periods.text: Clear, with a low around 50. Northwest wind 13 to 15 mph.

periods.name: Tuesday
periods.text: Sunny, with a high near 63. Northwest wind 9 to 11 mph.

periods.name: Tuesday Night
periods.text: Clear, with a low around 50. West wind 3 to 7 mph.

localgood.h: American chestnut returns to the Bronx Zoo
localgood.b: The Bronx Zoo is getting 25 blight-resistant chestnut saplings to help restore a tree nearly wiped out for over a century.
